subject: [hw] IV -> D01: FACTS candidates - vpud remap_shmem/vcu_inst_addr mechanism, ion fds in the encode message, VENC power before the first register write
body:
Three host-verified facts for FACTS.md (no phone; the vendor set is read at run time from gpu/build/cam-vendor-20261109/vfs):

[V] vpud remap_shmem() mechanism (bin/vpud, Thumb code at vaddr ~0x3200; strings at .rodata 0xe5d "remap_shmem", 0xf3a "[vpud] shmem_end %x shmem_start %x size %d", 0xf98 "libvpud_vcodec.so", 0xe72 "rw-p", 0x1410 "%x-%x"). It fopens /proc/self/maps and takes the FIRST line containing BOTH "rw-p" and "libvpud_vcodec.so"; sscanf "%x-%x" gives the mapping start/end. It mmaps the VCU DMEM (offset 0x80000000, length end-start), memcpy()s the range into it, munmaps, then mmaps offset 0x88000000 MAP_FIXED at the same start. The static codec tables it hands out (venc_get_addr) are libvpud_vcodec.so BSS/data: venc_drv_inst vaddr 0x85eb0 (0x5320 bytes), venc_formats 0x8b1d0 (0x300), venc_framesizes 0x8b4d0 (0x900) (llvm-nm -D + the function at 0x1128c). On Android the RELRO page is r--p, so the selected line is the data+bss PT_LOAD (vaddr 0x17d70, memsz 0x745e8), NOT the 0x3f0 .data.rel.ro page. The kernel's VCU_DMEM0_VMA is that mmap's vma->vm_start (mtk_vcu.c:1707-1711), and vcu_mapping_dm_addr() translates against it (:1199-1225), so vcu_inst_addr = venc_drv_inst is valid only if the COMMIT mmap landed at the data segment's page start. Evidence: IV maps fix in the tree -> vpud logs shmem_start 4009e000 size 483328; M-d accepted.

[V] The vendor ring buffer imports the dma-buf fds from venc_ap_ipi_msg_enc: with input_fd[0]=0/bs_fd=0 it logs "[ERROR] ion_import failed, ion_buf_fd = 0 LINE: 101" then "[ERROR] ringbuf get_ion_buffer_addr fail 0x00000000!!" and answers ENCODE_DONE status 0 with bs_size 0 (strings at libvpud_vcodec.so .rodata 0x3340/0x392d/0x60bd). With AP-registered V34 ion shares (0x500/0x501) in those fields the import and the whole VENC sequence run.

[V host; I phone] This daemon does not send VCU_IPIMSG_ENC_POWER_ON before its first VENC register write (host trace: first GCE op is W VENC 0x00a8, no 0xE000 message). The Linux AP powers the clocks in venc_encode_prepare() -> mtk_vcodec_enc_clock_on() from the POWER_ON handler (venc_vcu_if.c:135-148, venc_drv_if.c:109-124). With RWVC_POWER(VENC)+RWVC_POWER(VENC_C1) held by the AP around the job, the fake hardware accepts the write and the daemon writes 55 VENC registers and reaches wait_irq(RWVC_IRQ_VENC). Whether the phone daemon also skips POWER_ON [I] (the phone test will tell); the host runner now powers explicitly.
